current.text: He is the projected starting center for Toronto and the only seven-footer on the roster.
He is not in the expected closing five. Toronto plans to close with a small, switchable group that has Murray-Boyles at center.
Reports say he is in good shape this summer, and he looked good in a preseason game on 2026-10-04.
Experts lean optimistic about his health. One is not worried about the back unless it flares up again in training camp.
Last season he barely contested shots and blocked very little. He was effective in only about half of his games.
Experts blame the back injury for his bad season and hope his blocks come back.
Experts say the market ranks him too low. They see him as a good late flyer at bench cost, worth a look outside the top 100 if he is healthy.
If he plays about 28 minutes and the back caused the drop in blocks, he is an easy top 70 pick.
He went for 4 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
His 70% FG% last season came on low volume. An expert does not expect it to last.
He turned only 35% of his deflections into steals last season. An expert expects his steals to improve.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games. The bench is thin after a solid top seven.

durable.text: He is an elite finisher with a strong FG% on modest volume.
His free throw shooting has improved steadily. He is no longer a hack target, but it is still a mild drag.
He has lost a step on defense and is not an elite rim protector.
His back flared up repeatedly last season.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both value him at 2 USD (ranks 122 and 116), well below the 15 USD he cost in our league last season. Experts call that too low, and he went for 4 USD in an expert mock. That makes him a cheap late center who lifts FG% and fits punt 3PM builds, with a mild FT% drag. Early in the season, check whether he plays about 28 minutes, whether his blocks come back toward the 1.2 to 1.5 range he had before last season, and whether the back stays quiet.
